business.title: Efficient greybox fuzzing framework with tabu search
business.description: Recently, fuzzing has emerged as a prominent technique for automatically detecting a wide range of security vulnerabilities in cybersecurity. Nevertheless, existing fuzzers remain limited in seed scheduling and energy allocation, as they typically rely on coarse-grained criteria or computationally intensive methods to evaluate seed quality. In this paper, we propose a novel adaptive fuzzing framework, namely TabuFuzz, which aims to prioritize seeds with a higher likelihood of generating interesting variants through mutation and allocate more energy to that seed. Specifically, TabuFuzz utilizes a tabu search (TS) algorithm to model seed scheduling, enabling the precise selection of promising seeds. In addition, we design an adaptive energy allocation strategy that exploits fine-grained dynamic execution information, thereby enhancing overall fuzzing efficiency. We implement TabuFuzz on top of AFL and evaluate it on nine widely-used real-world programs. Across six independent 24-hour trials, TabuFuzz achieved higher observed path exploration and crash discovery than the evaluated baselines on most target programs, with improvements of 19.89% and 160.87% over AFL, respectively. Comparative analyses further show that TabuFuzz recorded higher numbers of paths and crashes than representative fuzzers such as FairFuzz, MOPT, EcoFuzz, and AFL + + under the reported experimental setup.

science.title: 'Stupendously large' primordial black holes ruled out as a dark matter source
science.description: Primordial black holes are hypothetical objects that could have formed directly from dense clumps of matter in the very early universe. If they exist, their dramatic origins would set them apart from the black holes we see today, which form when massive stars collapse. Some theories suggest that "stupendously large" primordial black holes could account for a significant share of the universe's elusive dark matter.
